article_title: Rust Stabilizes the Never Type, Shipping a Breaking Fallback Change Across All Editions in 1.100
summary: Human reviewer override: automated script found only an allowlist warning, but manual source verification found a pattern of unverifiable quotes, crate names, and statistics attributed to two GitHub PR comments and the PR's diffstat, none of which are present in the archived snapshots.

findings.message: Direct quote and PR-diffstat claim unverifiable against source-0 snapshot
findings.details: Body paragraph 2 claims the PR '428 files with 1,798 additions and 3,635 deletions, and drew 80 comments and 33 review comments before merging.' None of these numbers (428, 1798/1,798, 3635/3,635, 80, 33) appear anywhere in the plain-text extraction of sources/2026-09/rust-stabilizes-the-never-type-shipping-a-breaking-fallback-change-across-all-editions-in-1100/source-0.html.gz, which is the cited source for this sentence (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155499).

findings.message: Direct quote unverifiable — cited comment body not present in source-2 snapshot
findings.details: Body paragraph 3 quotes issuecomment-4290552375 as saying the compiler 'used to default such variables to `()`, which can cause confusing behavior, such as "spontaneously decaying" values of type `!` (especially around closures).' Neither this quote nor any of its distinctive terms ('decay'/'spontaneous'/'confusing behavior'/'libraries') appear in source-2.html.gz. Inspection of the raw HTML shows comment 4290552375 has no `id="issuecomment-4290552375"` anchor in the snapshot (only cross-reference links to it) — the actual comment body was never captured, likely because GitHub collapses long PR comment threads behind client-side pagination that a static fetch does not follow. The quote cannot be verified as verbatim or even paraphrased-correctly from any text in the snapshot.

findings.message: Direct quote, crate names, and figures unverifiable — cited comment body not present in source-1 snapshot
findings.details: Body paragraph 4 attributes a multi-sentence analysis to WaffleLapkin via issuecomment-4290467341, including two direct quotes ('practically all ~3K crater failures are coming from crates which depend on old versions of libraries, which already have a patched version'; 'have been receiving warnings for almost a year now'; 'without specifying type of the value requested'), a count ('Only seven crates broke directly...including one crate last updated seven years ago'), four specific crate names (redis-lock, rust-trending, alion-admin-api, cache-any), and a claim about sqlx-postgres. None of these strings (including loose keyword checks for 'libraries', 'redis', 'sqlx', 'decay'/'spontaneous') appear anywhere in source-1.html.gz. As with source-2, comment 4290467341 has no rendered `id="issuecomment-4290467341"` anchor in the snapshot — only cross-reference links to it exist. This is the single largest paragraph in the article and its entire evidentiary basis is unverifiable from the cited source.

content_preview.title: Rust Stabilizes the Never Type, Shipping a Breaking Fallback Change Across All Editions in 1.100
content_preview.summary: A decade-old proposal to make Rust's ! type official merged August 24, 2026, targeting Rust 1.100.0 and breaking about 3,277 crates in ecosystem-wide testing.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Rust's "never" type — written `!` and used to mark functions and expressions that can never return a value — was stabilized on August 24, 2026, when contributor WaffleLapkin's pull request ["stabilize never type"](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155499) merged into the compiler. The change is targeted at Rust 1.100.0, according to the milestone attached to the merged pull request, and it closes a tracking issue that had been open on GitHub since July 2016.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece with a clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure, appropriate technical register for a Rust-developer audience, and no AI self-reference or sensationalism. The prose quality itself is not the problem with this submission.
editor_notes.source_verification: Verified integrity of all 10 snapshots first: decompressed each of sources/2026-09/rust-stabilizes-the-never-type-shipping-a-breaking-fallback-change-across-all-editions-in-1100/source-{0..9}.html.gz and recomputed sha256 — all 10 hashes match manifest.json exactly, so the files reviewed are the exact bytes fetched. suspicious_patterns is null on every entry; no prompt-injection concern. Content verification per source: (1) source-0, PR#155499 base page — confirms title 'stabilize never type' by WaffleLapkin, the four-part PR description (stabilizes never type, sets fallback to `!` on all editions as a breaking change, makes Infallible an alias to `!`, removes dependency_on_unit_never_type_fallback lint) — all CONFIRMED. However the diffstat sentence ('428 files... 1,798 additions... 3,635 deletions... 80 comments... 33 review comments') is NOT FOUND anywhere in the plain-text extraction of this snapshot — UNVERIFIED. (2) source-1, issuecomment-4290467341 (cited as 'analysis') — the comment ID appears only as a hyperlink target within the PR description and other comments; there is no `id="issuecomment-4290467341"` anchor with rendered body content in this snapshot. None of the article's quoted text or supporting details (two direct quotes, 4 crate names: redis-lock/rust-trending/alion-admin-api/cache-any, sqlx-postgres mention, 'seven crates'/'seven years' figures) appear anywhere in the file, including loose case-insensitive keyword scans for 'libraries', 'redis', 'sqlx', 'decay' — UNVERIFIED, comment body was never captured. (3) source-2, issuecomment-4290552375 (cited as 'refresher on never type fallback') — same situation: no rendered comment anchor, and the quoted text ('used to default such variables to (), which can cause confusing behavior, such as "spontaneously decaying" values...') does not appear anywhere in the snapshot — UNVERIFIED. (4) source-3, issuecomment-4279084886 (crater report) — this comment DOES have a rendered `id="issuecomment-4279084886"` anchor with full body text; confirmed verbatim: 'Experiment pr-155499 is completed! 3277 regressed and 0 fixed (9024 total)' and '1149 spurious results' — CONFIRMED, matches article precisely, including the 'What We Don't Know' mention of the 1,149 spurious results. (5) source-4, PR#123508 — confirms title 'Edition 2024: Make ! fall back to !', merged, 'Jun 12, 2024' — CONFIRMED. (6) source-5, PR#65355 — confirms title 'Stabilize ! in Rust 1.41.0', merged, 'Nov 21, 2019' — CONFIRMED. (7) source-6, PR#67224 — confirms title 'Revert stabilization of never type', merged, 'Dec 15, 2019' — CONFIRMED. (8) source-7, issue#35121 — confirms 'Tracking issue for promoting ! to a type (RFC 1216)', 'nikomatsakis opened on Jul 29, 2016' — CONFIRMED (article's 'July 2016' is accurate); the '378 comments' figure could not be located in the text (same category of limitation as the diffstat counts) — UNVERIFIED but minor and not quote-based. (9) source-8, doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.never.html — confirms verbatim 'the canonical uninhabited type' and 'the type of diverging computations – computations which never resolve to any value', and page header shows 'std 1.100.0-nightly' — CONFIRMED, exact quote match. (10) source-9, edition-guide/rust-2024/never-type-fallback.html — confirms the 2024-edition fallback-to-`!` change described in the article — CONFIRMED.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Six of ten sources check out cleanly, including an exact match on the crater-test regression figures (3,277 regressed / 0 fixed / 9,024 total / 1,149 spurious — precisely as the submission states) and exact verbatim matches on the doc.rust-lang.org quotes. However, two sources (source-1 and source-2) are cited for a combined ~40% of the 'What We Know' section — including two direct quotes in quotation marks attributed by name to a real person (WaffleLapkin), four specific crate names, and several numeric claims — and none of that content is present in the archived snapshots. Inspection of the raw HTML shows the two cited GitHub comment IDs never received a rendered comment body in the snapshot (only cross-reference links to them exist elsewhere on the page), which is consistent with GitHub collapsing long PR threads behind client-side-only pagination that a static fetch does not follow. That explains the mechanism, but does not change the review obligation: content attributed to these sources, including verbatim-quoted material, cannot be confirmed as accurate, paraphrased-correctly, or even genuine from anything available in the provenance record. A third, smaller issue (source-0's diffstat/comment-count sentence) has the same unverifiable character.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no editorializing or loaded language.
editor_notes.originality: No article on Rust's never-type stabilization exists in src/content/articles/2026-09/ or recent months (checked via grep across src/content/articles/ for 'never type', 'issuecomment', and 'WaffleLapkin' — no hits). This is a genuinely new topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: The PR-diffstat/comment-count sentence in paragraph 2 (428 files, 1,798 additions, 3,635 deletions, 80 comments, 33 review comments) is not supported by any text in source-0's snapshot.

The direct quote attributed to issuecomment-4290552375 in paragraph 3 ('used to default such variables to (), which can cause confusing behavior, such as "spontaneously decaying" values of type ! (especially around closures)') is not present anywhere in source-2's snapshot; the cited comment body was never captured.

Paragraph 4 — the article's longest paragraph — attributes two direct quotes, four specific crate names (redis-lock, rust-trending, alion-admin-api, cache-any), a mention of sqlx-postgres, and several numeric claims ('seven crates', 'seven years') to issuecomment-4290467341, none of which appear anywhere in source-1's snapshot; the cited comment body was never captured.

Taken together, this is not a single recoverable misattribution but a pattern spanning two of the article's four GitHub-comment-level citations and covering roughly two full paragraphs of substantive, quote-bearing content — more than a single honest corrections note can responsibly summarize for readers.
recommendations: If this topic is resubmitted, the contributor bot should either quote only what is directly visible in a fresh, fully-loaded fetch of the specific comment permalinks (verifying the comment's own `id=` anchor is present in whatever snapshot mechanism is used), or drop any claim it cannot re-confirm against a re-fetched, fully-rendered version of the long PR thread.

Consider flagging to the pipeline maintainers that GitHub PR/issue snapshots may silently omit large ranges of mid-thread comments (client-side pagination) even when status_code is 200 and no error is recorded — this is a blind spot the manifest does not currently surface, since 'file' being non-null gives false confidence that the cited comment was actually captured.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The crater-test regression figures and doc.rust-lang.org quotes are verified precisely, and the article is well-written and neutral, but roughly two paragraphs of substantive content — including two named direct quotes, four specific crate names, and several numeric claims — are attributed to two GitHub PR comments whose actual bodies are absent from the archived snapshots and cannot be verified by any means available in this review. This is a pattern across multiple specifics tied to real named quotes, not a single recoverable slip, and exceeds what a single corrections note can honestly cover per the v3.9.0 policy. The bot should research and resubmit with re-verifiable sourcing for the crater-failure root-cause analysis and the fallback-mechanism explanation.
